original_question: The function dn(σ, τ) = (1/n)·|{x ∈ {1,..., n} | σ(x) ̸= τ (x)}| is a distance on the symmetric group Sn. For a finitely generated group G, an almost-homomorphism is a sequence of set-theoretic maps fn: G → Sn satisfying dn(fn(g)fn(h), fn(gh)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g, h ∈ G. An almost-homomorphism {fn } is said to be close to a homomorphism if there is a sequence of group homomorphisms ρn: G → Sn such that dn(ρn(g), fn(g)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g ∈ G. The group G is said to be permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of G is close to a homomorphism. Conjecture: Metabelian groups are permutation-stable.

refined_question: Let G be a finitely generated metabelian group. For each n >= 1, let S_n be the symmetric group on {1, ..., n}, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance d_n(σ, τ) = (1/n)|{x in {1, ..., n} : σ(x) != τ(x)}|. Suppose {f_n} is a sequence of set-theoretic maps f_n: G -> S_n such that d_n(f_n(g)f_n(h), f_n(gh)) -> 0 as n -> infinity for every g, h in G. Must there exist a sequence of group homomorphisms rho_n: G -> S_n such that d_n(rho_n(g), f_n(g)) -> 0 as n -> infinity for every g in G? Equivalently: is every finitely generated metabelian group permutation-stable?
